title: Ctrl+S in verb editor throws UnauthorizedAccessException (saves to Program Files)
description:
Critical: pressing Ctrl+S (File > Save) in a local-edit verb editor throws System.UnauthorizedAccessException and the app shows the unhandled-exception dialog. The verb code is not saved.

Observed exception:
System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path
'C:\Program Files\Moo Udditor\ANSI Utilities:notify - SRTMoo-0dcc69b6-2d0c-46c7-aeb4-31f9c0d61d9f' is denied.
  at FastColoredTextBoxNS.Text.TextSource.SaveToFile(...)
  at FastColoredTextBoxNS.FastColoredTextBox.SaveToFile(...)
  at Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor.Main.Editor.mnuItemSave_Click(...) in Editor_FileMenu.cs:line 73

Repro:
- Open a verb via the server local-edit flow (e.g. "ANSI Utilities:notify" on world SRTMoo).
- Press Ctrl+S.

ROOT CAUSE (two intertwined defects):
1. Document.Path is set to a non-path identifier. In MooCodeEditorPage's local-edit constructor (Pages/MooCodeEditorPage.cs ~line 74-80):
     var name = $"{verbName} - {worldName}";
     var key  = $"{name}-{Guid.NewGuid()}";
     Editor.Document = new DocumentInfo(key, key, verbName);   // <- path == key
   The DocumentInfo's *path* is set to `key` (a window/document identifier: "<verb> - <world>-<guid>"), not a real file path. mnuItemSave_Click (Editor_FileMenu.cs:72-73) then does:
     if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(page.Document.Path))
        page.SourceEditor.SaveToFile(page.Document.Path, Encoding.Default);
   Because `key` is a RELATIVE path, SaveToFile resolves it against the current working directory = the install dir (C:\Program Files\Moo Udditor), which is not writable for standard users (we now install to 64-bit Program Files) -> UnauthorizedAccessException.

2. The name contains characters illegal in Windows file paths. MOO verb references use object:verb syntax, so `verbName` = "ANSI Utilities:notify" contains a colon. Even in a writable directory, ':' is treated as an NTFS alternate-data-stream separator; other refs can contain \ / * ? " < > | as well. Any filename derived from a verb reference must be sanitized.

EXPECTED / FIX DIRECTION:
- A local-edit verb document has no on-disk file. Ctrl+S on such a document should NOT write the document key to disk. Preferred: Ctrl+S on a verb page performs the verb UPLOAD back to the server (the existing LocalEditUploader flow), not a FastColoredTextBox file save.
- If/when saving to disk is intended (e.g. Save As, or a working copy), it must (a) use a writable location (%APPDATA%\Moo Udditor or Path.GetTempPath()) and (b) sanitize the filename of all Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() (notably ':').
- Stop assigning `key` to DocumentInfo.Path. Either leave Path empty (so Save routes to Save-As) or assign a proper sanitized, writable path. Distinguish "verb document (upload target)" from "on-disk file document" so Save does the right thing per type.

Affected files: Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor/Main/Editor_FileMenu.cs (mnuItemSave_Click ~line 68-85), Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor/Pages/MooCodeEditorPage.cs (~line 74-80, DocumentInfo path = key), DocumentInfo model, and the local-edit upload path (Communication/OutOfBand/LocalEditUploader.cs).

Severity: critical — crashes via unhandled exception and loses the user's verb edits on a primary, very common action (save). Surfaced by the move to installing under Program Files (non-writable CWD), but the underlying path/identifier confusion is the real bug.

Source: user bug report with full stack trace (assembly version 1.0.26158.7).
notes:
Save-location decision: the default root for new save files should be the user's My Documents folder (Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments / Personal), e.g. a 'Moo Udditor' subfolder under My Documents (which is user-writable, unlike the Program Files install dir). The Save As dialog's InitialDirectory should default there, and filenames must still be sanitized of Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars (notably ':'). Note this is distinct from per-user app data (config/snippets/worlds/logs), which lives in %APPDATA%/Moo Udditor; user-facing saved .moo files belong under My Documents.
CLARIFICATION (supersedes 'fix direction' item 1 in the description): Ctrl+S is INTENDED to save a COPY of the verb code to local disk. It is NOT meant to upload to the server (that is a separate action). So the correct fix is: keep Ctrl+S as a file save, but fix WHERE and WHAT it saves. Because a freshly local-edited verb document has no real on-disk path yet, the current code wrongly uses the window 'key' as Document.Path. Instead: when Document.Path is not a real saved file, Ctrl+S routes to Save As, with the dialog InitialDirectory defaulting to My Documents/Moo Udditor and a suggested file name = the sanitized verb reference (replace Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars, notably ':') with a .moo extension. After the user saves once, store the chosen real path in Document.Path so subsequent Ctrl+S overwrites that file silently. Never assign the window key to DocumentInfo.Path.
close_reason: Fixed: stopped storing the window key in DocumentInfo.Path (root cause of the relative-path save into Program Files); Ctrl+S now saves a local copy via Save As defaulting to My Documents/Moo Udditor with a sanitized filename, overwriting silently after first save. Saves go through TrySaveToFile (logs + MessageBox, no crash); PromptForSave (close prompt) hardened identically; SanitizeFileName handles invalid chars, trailing dots/spaces, reserved device names. Independently reviewed; builds clean.

title: Snippet autocomplete matches longer snippet first
description:
Critical: during autocomplete, snippet matching selects a longer snippet over the exact/shorter one. Typing a token matches a snippet that merely has it as a prefix instead of the snippet that exactly matches.

Repro:
- Type "for" -> matches the "Fork" snippet instead of the "for" snippet.
- Type "else" -> matches the "elseif" snippet instead of the "else" snippet.

Expected:
- An exact match should win over a longer prefix match. Typing "for" should select "for", "else" should select "else". Longer snippets (Fork, elseif) should only be offered when the typed text is actually a prefix of only those, or ranked below the exact match.

Notes:
- Likely a snippet match ordering/selection issue in the autocomplete matching logic (see Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Editor/Autocomplete and Snippets handling). Candidate ordering should prioritize exact matches, then shortest/most-specific, rather than first/longest.
- Case sensitivity may also be involved ("for" vs "Fork").

Source: user report.
close_reason: Fixed: autocomplete now ranks exact match first, then shortest, then source order; exact matches no longer hidden. 'for'->'for', 'else'->'else'. Implemented in FastColoredTextBox fork (AutocompleteItem.Compare + AutocompleteMenu.DoAutocomplete), independently reviewed, builds clean.

title: Refactor edgerunner-org-moo-query send_reply/send_error to use core MCP framework send (fixes auth-key=0 reply drop)
description: send_reply (line 443) and send_error (line 465) hand-roll the MCP wire format via notify('#$#'...) and stamp session.key, which resolves to 0 on EdgeRunner cores (the negotiated client key is on .authentication_key). The core MCP framework already does key-stamping, package-prefix, and multiline data* chunking via connection:send(message, parse_send_args(...)) — exactly as #215:send_* and the simpleedit reference (#230) use it. Refactor both verbs to delegate to the framework instead of reinventing the wire format. Root cause of member-completion popup never appearing for $foo: contexts (replies discarded by McpMessageDispatcher key check).

title: Member autocomplete popup never opens on first trigger (results land after menu closed)
description: When the user types 'obj:' / 'obj.' / '$name:' the trigger keystroke runs DoAutocomplete while the member fetch is still in flight; GetMemberItems returns empty, no static item matches the fragment, and AutocompleteMenu closes (Count==0 -> Menu.Close). When the fetch lands, the MooCodeEditorPage menuRefresh callback only re-shows a VISIBLE menu (menu is { Visible: true }), so the popup never opens — user must type another character. Fix: when the menu is closed and the caret still sits in a member context with non-empty fetched items, open the menu (Show(false)) from the refresh callback, guarded by editor focus. Also: MemberCompletionController swallows all provider failures silently with no logging anywhere in the Editor project — add an optional diagnostic callback invoked on fetch failure and core-name validation failure, wired to NLog in MooCodeEditorPage, so field failures are diagnosable.
notes: Scope addition: McpMessageDispatcher.cs:83 silently drops messages whose auth key mismatches Session.Key — log a WARN naming message name + both keys. This silent drop cost a full debugging session (server sent key 0; replies dropped; queries timed out). Root cause of user's $network: failure was server-side: core session object stores auth key in a property other than .key (send_reply emitted 0).
close_reason: Popup-show fix + dispatcher WARN + diagnostic callback implemented, reviewed, approved

title: Autocomplete does not open for $name member operands ($network:)
description: MemberOperandResolver only resolves #N literals and 'this' for Verb/Property contexts; $name operands (e.g. $network:) return null and MemberCompletionController silently skips member completion — no query is sent, popup never opens. Fix: resolve $name client-side via GetPropertyValueAsync(#0, name) (prop-value op returns {"t":1,"v":"#N"}), cache name→objnum with TTL, then run the normal verb/prop fetch. Covers both $name: and $name. forms. No server-side changes needed.
close_reason: Closed

title: MCP multiline content double-spaced: parser retains transport newline in continuation values
description:
Surfaced testing simpleedit @edit: verb code opens in the editor with a blank line between every line (unusable).

Root cause: the OOB transport delivers each line with a trailing newline (MudClientSession.FlushLine appends "
"). RootMessageProcessor strips only the #$# prefix, not the newline, so McpMessageParser.FeedLine receives lines ending in "
". ProcessMultilineLine preserves the continuation value literally (to keep indentation), INCLUDING the trailing "
", then assembles with string.Join("
", lines) -> each line becomes 'code
' and the join inserts another '
', producing a blank line between every content line. Single-line messages are unaffected because ProcessNormalLine goes through SplitMessageIntoWords which trims.

Fix: strip a single trailing line terminator (one '
', plus a preceding '' if present) at the top of McpMessageParser.FeedLine before dispatching to the normal/multiline handlers, so the parser tolerates the transport newline. Add a parser test feeding newline-terminated continuation lines and asserting single-newline join.
close_reason: Verified working against EdgeRunner: @edit opens the verb, code is single-spaced with indentation intact, and round-trip save programs the verb. (Blank-line stripping confirmed to be MOO server compile/decompile behavior, not a client bug.)

title: Network read loop splits long OOB lines across 10KB chunks, breaking MCP multiline
description:
Regression surfaced by enabling dns-org-mud-moo-simpleedit (udd-wm8): @edit on a connected MOO opens no editor.

Root cause (confirmed via Moo Udditor.log): MudClientSession.ReadFromConnection reads in 10240-byte chunks and calls FlushCommandBuffer() after EVERY chunk (MudClientSession.cs:342). FlushCommandBuffer (line 440) flushes any unterminated partial line (needed so no-newline prompts display). When a long line spans a 10KB read boundary it gets emitted as two channel messages: the first half (still #$#-prefixed) and the remainder (no prefix). Mid-MCP-multiline, RootMessageProcessor delegates the prefix-less remainder to McpOobHandler, whose parser is in multiline state and returns Error on a line that is neither '* ...' nor ': ...', which resets the parser and sets Finished=true -> the entire simpleedit content message is aborted -> no editor. Log shows the 'Resetting message processor' cascade starting exactly where a long verb line ('player:tell(...)') was truncated to '...content: p'.

Fix: in ReadFromConnection, only call FlushCommandBuffer() when the read drained the socket (bytes < buffer.Length); a full-buffer read means more of the current line is likely still coming, so keep accumulating until the newline (FlushLine) so multi-chunk lines reassemble intact. Prompts (short reads) still flush. Stream-agnostic (also fixes TLS) and testable with a scripted stream.

Affects all connections (core networking). Pre-existing latent issue adjacent to docs/terminal-buffer-cutoff-investigation.md Issue 3; exposed now because @edit routes through MCP multiline.
close_reason: Verified working against EdgeRunner: @edit opens the verb, code is single-spaced with indentation intact, and round-trip save programs the verb. (Blank-line stripping confirmed to be MOO server compile/decompile behavior, not a client bug.)

title: Autocomplete popup crashes at high editor zoom (no font-size ceiling)
description:
Typing with autocomplete open after zooming the editor up throws System.ArgumentException 'Parameter is not valid' from System.Drawing.Font.GetHeight, via AutocompleteListView.ItemHeight -> ApplyZoom -> DoAutocomplete (AutocompleteMenu.cs:194/325/399).

Root cause: AutocompletePopupMetrics.Compute (FastColoredTextBox/AutocompletePopupMetrics.cs) floors the effective font size at MinFontSizeInPoints (6pt) but applies NO upper ceiling. The editor's own FastColoredTextBox.DoZoom guards 'points < 1f || points > 300f', but FastColoredTextBox.Zoom's setter stores the raw zoom field even when DoZoom bails out of range. So at high zoom tb.Zoom keeps climbing while the editor font caps at 300pt; the popup recomputes baseFont(9pt) * zoom/100 unbounded and asks GDI+ for a degenerate (huge) font. GDI+ returns a Font with an invalid native handle, so Font.Height throws.

Repro: zoom the editor up substantially, then type so autocomplete fires. Also reproduced after tabbing away/back with an already-high zoom.

Fix: clamp the computed font size to a sane maximum (mirror the editor's 300pt cap) in AutocompletePopupMetrics.Compute, plus a unit test for the high-zoom cap.
design: Build effective font from family name (not FontFamily object) to decouple lifetime; snapshot family name/size/style at assignment time while the source font is still valid.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (verified by reproduction test ShowMenu_ThenZoom_ThenReshow_DoesNotCrash): AutocompleteListView built its effective (zoomed) font from baseFont.FontFamily. When the ToolStripControlHost/ambient-font machinery pushes its own Font onto the list view (through the overridden Font setter, which resets baseFont) and WinForms later disposes that pushed font, every font sharing its FontFamily is invalidated -> Font.Height throws 'Parameter is not valid'. Triggered on ANY zoom change followed by the menu becoming visible (DoSelectedVisible/DoAutocomplete). The missing font-size ceiling (original hypothesis) was NOT the cause; that clamp was kept as a secondary safety.

FIX (FastColoredTextBox/AutocompleteMenu.cs): capture the baseline font identity (family NAME string, point size, style) into immutable fields whenever baseFont is assigned, and rebuild the effective font from the family NAME so each effective font owns its own family and is immune to WinForms disposing the pushed font. Plus defensive guards: try/catch in ApplyZoom font creation and in ItemHeight. Verified: the repro test failed before the fix and passes after; full FCTB test suite 12/12 green; main app builds.
close_reason: Fixed: ApplyZoom disposed the live base.Font when Control.Font ignored an equal-by-value reassignment. Now only swaps+disposes when the font actually differs. Verified by forced-paint repro test (host-crash before, passes after) and confirmed working in-app by user.

title: Autocomplete: resolve this/player/caller as known member-completion sources
description:
Add the predefined Moo variables 'this', 'player', and 'caller' as known operands for member (verb/property) autocomplete AND hover tooltips, resolving to their DEFAULT objects. STATIC default resolution only — dynamic reassignment tracking is the follow-up udd-efk.

- 'this' -> the object the edited verb lives on (the page's ContextObjectId). MemberOperandResolver already maps 'this' -> contextObjectId; verify end-to-end for verbs AND properties through both the completion popup and the hover-tooltip operand resolution.
- 'player' and 'caller' -> default to the current connected player object. Add a method to IMooWorldQueryProvider (e.g. GetCurrentPlayerAsync) and implement it in McpQueryProvider, SdwcQueryProvider, the MooWorldQueryProviderRegistry aggregate, and the server-side edgerunner-org-moo-query package (a new message returning the connected player's object id). Wire MemberOperandResolver / MemberCompletionController and the MooCodeEditorPage hover operand resolution to resolve player/caller via this query (and reset on disconnect, per udd-bju).

Touch points: MemberOperandResolver, MemberCompletionController, IMooWorldQueryProvider (+ MCP/SDWC impls + server query package + protocol doc), MooCodeEditorPage hover operand resolution.
close_reason: Phase 1 (static default resolution) implemented + tested: GetCurrentPlayerAsync across provider/registry/MCP (+ handle_player server verb); player/caller resolve to the connected player in completion + hover; this verified. Reassignment/chained exprs remain udd-efk.

title: Investigate SDWC capability line shadowed by MCP handler ordering
description: In WindowManager.CreateTerminalPage the McpOobHandler is registered before SdwcOobHandler. During disconnect-teardown work it was observed that McpOobHandler consumes the bare 'dome-client-user' SDWC capability line first (its parser treats it as a complete, unknown MCP message), so SdwcOobHandler may never see it and never register the SDWC query provider in production. Confirm whether SDWC registration is actually shadowed, and if so fix the handler ordering or make MCP not consume non-MCP OOB lines.

title: Editor hover tooltips for verbs/properties (doc / value)
description: Mouse-hover over a verb/property reference token in the Moo code editor shows a tooltip above the cursor: verb documentation (GetVerbDocumentationAsync) for verbs, '.name => value' (GetPropertyValueAsync) for properties. Phase 1 (this): FCTB HoverWordPattern support + temp handler showing the hovered token to prove the hover plumbing. Phase 2: parse the reference at the hovered place, resolve the object, query, and show real content.

title: Distinguish inherited vs local members in autocomplete popup (gold-chevron badge)
description: Add an optional MemberOrigin (Unknown/Local/Inherited) to MooVerbSummary/MooPropertySummary. MCP server emits per-row [name,isLocal]; MCP mapping sets Origin; SDWC maps to Unknown (interface stays SDWC-compatible). Inherited verb/property icons render the existing purple/cyan icon plus a gold up-chevron badge with a dark halo (colorblind-safe structural cue). Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-22-inherited-member-icons-design.md
close_reason: Gold up-arrow inherited badge implemented; user approved at 75% size, lower-right

title: Replace tonum() with toint() in query package dump
description: Thad: tonum() is not valid on the EdgeRunner server (ToastStunt lineage dropped the old LambdaMOO alias). Replace all 12 occurrences (10 code + 2 doc-comment) in Server Packages/edgerunner-org-moo-query.moo with toint(), which is valid on both LambdaMOO 1.8+ and ToastStunt.
close_reason: All tonum() replaced with toint() in the dump; toint is valid on both LambdaMOO 1.8+ and ToastStunt.

title: Make edgerunner-org-moo-query dump self-contained (@prop/@verb commands)
description: Thad: the @verb commands should be IN the dump file, not a manual INSTALL step. Add @prop lines for the six metadata properties and @verb lines for all 17 verbs to Server Packages/edgerunner-org-moo-query.moo (before the ;; assignments / @args blocks), so a search-replace of #XXX plus a paste is a complete install. Inherited properties will make @prop report a harmless 'already defined' error. Update INSTALL.md to drop the manual create-verbs step and note the harmless errors.
close_reason: Dump now creates its own properties (@prop) and verbs (@verb); INSTALL simplified.

title: MCP version negotiation is culture-sensitive (breaks on comma-decimal locales)
description: Found during udd-btl final review, pre-existing (commits 4a0189f/4320c69): McpMessageDispatcher.cs:125-126 formats package versions with MinimumVersion.ToString("F1") and McpNegotiatePackage.cs:97-98 parses with double.TryParse, both using the current culture. On a comma-decimal locale (e.g. German Windows) the client advertises 'min-version: 1,0' and cannot parse the server's '1.0', so no MCP package (simpleedit, edgerunner-org-moo-query) ever activates. Fix: use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture at both call sites; consider an invariant-culture round-trip test.

title: Unregister MOO query providers and fail pending requests on disconnect
description: Code review of McpQueryPackage (udd-btl Task 6) found there is no session-teardown path: nothing calls QueryProviders.Unregister when a terminal connection ends, McpQueryPackage.Reset() is an empty no-op nobody calls, and pending McpQueryCorrelator entries dangle until their bounded timeout. After disconnect a consumer hitting QueryProviders.Query still routes to McpQueryProvider, which calls SendOutOfBandLine on a dead terminal — either throwing raw to the consumer or burning the full 10s timeout per call. Same pattern likely applies to SdwcQueryProvider. Fix: wire a disconnect/teardown hook (natural home may be adding Reset() to IMcpPackage and invoking it on session end) that unregisters providers and faults pending correlator entries.
close_reason: Implemented hybrid disconnect teardown: OnDisconnected cascade off Closed (unregister providers + FaultAll pending with QueryConnectionClosedException) + IDisposable safety net. Merged to master, all suites green.

title: Rename GetObjectsAsync to GetCoreObjectsAsync across query provider stack
description: The operation only ever returns core ($-registered) objects per the udd-btl design, so the name GetObjects is misleading. Rename interface method, all implementations (registry, caching, SDWC), caching Operation enum value, test fakes/tests, and update the udd-btl spec wire messages (-objects -> -core-objects, handle_objects -> handle_core_objects) plus the 2026-06-07 interface design doc.
close_reason: Renamed across interface, registry, caching provider, SDWC provider, test fakes/tests, and specs; merged to master

title: Carry queried + resolved object ids on verb doc/code/info query results (inherited-verb resolution)
description:
A verb queried on an object may be inherited from an ancestor; callers need to know which object the verb actually lives on. Change IMooWorldQueryProvider so verb results carry both the queried object id and the resolved (defining) object id.

Changes (interface has no external consumers yet — break freely; fix our own code: registry, caching decorator, test fakes/tests):
- New record MooVerbDocumentation(MooObjectId QueriedObjectId, MooObjectId ResolvedObjectId, IReadOnlyList<string> Lines); GetVerbDocumentationAsync -> Task<MooVerbDocumentation?>.
- New record MooVerbCode(MooObjectId QueriedObjectId, MooObjectId ResolvedObjectId, IReadOnlyList<string> Lines); GetVerbCodeAsync -> Task<MooVerbCode?>.
- MooVerbInfo: add QueriedObjectId; rename DefiningObject -> ResolvedObjectId. GetVerbInfoAsync stays Task<MooVerbInfo?>.
- Registry: GetVerbDocumentationAsync/GetVerbCodeAsync move from list-style (empty on exhaustion) to nullable-single style (null on exhaustion), matching GetVerbInfoAsync.
- Caching decorator + FakeProviders + Mud.Common.Tests updated; all green.

Follow-up to udd-5oh.
close_reason: Implemented: MooVerbDocumentation/MooVerbCode result records and MooVerbInfo now carry QueriedObjectId + ResolvedObjectId (inherited-verb resolution). Interface, registry (doc/code now nullable-single), caching, fakes, and tests updated; 46 Mud.Common tests pass, editor builds clean.

title: MCP package enable/disable management page (global + per-world)
description:
Add a UI page/dialog where the user can enable or disable each MCP package that Udditor supports, so they can opt out of packages they don't want active.

Why: Udditor advertises/accepts a set of MCP (Mud Client Protocol) packages during negotiation. Users need control over which packages are active rather than always enabling everything.

Scope:
- A new 'MCP Packages' page/dialog (e.g. under the View menu, alongside Theme/Options) that lists every MCP package Udditor supports, each with an enable/disable toggle and a short description.
- Two levels of configuration:
  1. GLOBAL default - applies to all worlds unless overridden.
  2. PER-WORLD override - each world can override the global setting per package. Support tri-state per world: Inherit global / Force enabled / Force disabled.
- Persistence: global defaults in the application config; per-world overrides in the world configuration (Org.Edgerunner.Mud.Common/WorldConfiguration.cs, surfaced via WorldConfigurator/WorldManager). 
- Integration: MCP negotiation (Org.Edgerunner.Mud.MCP - McpClientSessionManager / McpOobHandler / IMcpPackage implementations such as SimpleEditPackage) must only offer/accept packages that are enabled for the connecting world (per-world override else global default). Disabled packages must not be negotiated or handled.
- Discoverability: the supported-package list should be derived from the registered IMcpPackage implementations so it stays in sync as packages are added.

Out of scope: implementing new MCP packages; changing the MCP handshake/negotiation protocol itself beyond filtering by the enabled set.
acceptance_criteria:
- An MCP Packages page can be opened and lists all supported packages with enable/disable controls.
- Global enable/disable of a package persists and takes effect for worlds with no override.
- A world can override any package to Inherit/Enabled/Disabled, persisted with the world config.
- During MCP negotiation for a connection, only packages enabled for that world (override else global) are offered/accepted; disabled packages are not negotiated or handled.
- The package list reflects the actual registered IMcpPackage implementations.

title: McpMessageParser multiline parsing uses wrong data-tag convention
description:
Defect in the udd-q2l deliverable. McpMessageParser's multiline handling assumes the data-tag is the value written after a keyword ending in '*:' (e.g. 'content*: <tag>'). The real MCP 2.1 model is different:

- The inline value after 'content*:' is syntactically required but IGNORED (conventionally "").
- The message line carries a single separate '_data-tag:' keyword whose value is the tag for the WHOLE message.
- Continuation lines are '#$#* <data-tag> <keyword>: <value>' and route to fields BY KEYWORD; multiple multiline fields in one message share the same data-tag.
- Close line is '#$#: <data-tag>'.

Current parser keys its multiline buffers by the (empty) inline value and looks up continuation lines by tag, so real server multiline messages (incl. dns-org-mud-moo-simpleedit-content) parse with an empty buffer and the actual content lines are dropped.

Fix: rework ProcessNormalLine/ProcessMultilineLine to (1) mark keywords ending in '*:' as multiline fields keyed by field name, ignoring their inline value, (2) read the single '_data-tag:' simple field as the message tag, (3) route continuation lines by matching tag + keyword, (4) close on ': <tag>'. Add tests covering the canonical MCP 2.1 example.

Also fix docs/mcp2-protocol.md which wrongly states each multiline field uses a different data-tag; per spec there is one _data-tag per message.

Blocks udd-wm8 (simpleedit content/set are multiline).
close_reason: Implemented on feature/mcp-simpleedit: udd-u5v fixes McpMessageParser to the MCP 2.1 _data-tag multiline model; udd-wm8 adds the dns-org-mud-moo-simpleedit package (SimpleEditPackage + SimpleEditUploader + FormatMultilineMessage + WindowManager wiring). 62 MCP tests pass, Udditor builds. Live round-trip verification against EdgeRunner still pending.

title: MCP local-edit package (round-trip verb edit via MCP)
description:
Implement a concrete MCP (MUD Client Protocol 2.1) edit package as an IMcpPackage so verb/code edits can round-trip via negotiated MCP rather than the current #$# OOB LocalEditHandler/LocalEditUploader fallback. This is the round-trip local-edit workflow that motivated udd-q2l; udd-q2l delivered the underlying mcp-negotiate + mcp-cord plumbing (now complete), but no concrete edit package exists yet.

MCP here = MUD Client Protocol, NOT the LLM Model Context Protocol.

Scope:
- Design the edit package message set (package name/version, e.g. an mcp-edit / dns-* package: edit-name, content multiline, set/upload messages).
- Implement as IMcpPackage participating in mcp-negotiate; handle inbound edit-open requests and outbound upload of edited code.
- Bridge to the existing editor local-edit UI (MooCodeEditorPage) so an MCP-initiated edit opens an editor page and the upload path sends code back over the negotiated session.
- Tests for message parse/format round-trip and negotiation participation.

Depends on udd-q2l (mcp-negotiate/mcp-cord plumbing, done).
close_reason: Implemented on feature/mcp-simpleedit: udd-u5v fixes McpMessageParser to the MCP 2.1 _data-tag multiline model; udd-wm8 adds the dns-org-mud-moo-simpleedit package (SimpleEditPackage + SimpleEditUploader + FormatMultilineMessage + WindowManager wiring). 62 MCP tests pass, Udditor builds. Live round-trip verification against EdgeRunner still pending.

title: Code hints + gutter code-action icon in the editor
description:
Today the editor only surfaces raw parser/syntax errors (via ParsingCompleteEventArgs -> ParserMessageDisplayPage). This feature adds a richer in-editor diagnostics/assist layer, in two related parts:

1. Code hints — display more than raw syntax errors: informational/warning hints, suggestions, and contextual diagnostics inline in the code editor windows (e.g. squiggles/markers + hover or inline hint text), layered on top of the existing ANTLR parse results so non-error insights (style, deprecations, unused locals, dialect-specific suggestions) can be shown without being treated as hard errors.

2. Gutter code-action icon — a clickable action affordance (lightbulb-style) drawn in the editor gutter/margin on lines that have an available action. Triggering it opens a menu of context actions such as refactorings (rename, extract, inline, quick-fixes for a hint). Actions are produced by the same diagnostics layer that feeds the hints.

The two parts share a model: a diagnostics/hint provider yields hints (some with attached actions); hints render as markers, actionable lines get the gutter icon, and invoking the icon runs the chosen action.
design: Build on existing pieces: the per-change background parse already raises ParsingCompleteEventArgs; extend that pipeline to emit non-error hints alongside errors instead of only errors. Render hints via FastColoredTextBox styles/markers (the fork already supports custom gutter/margin drawing and bookmark-style icons — same surface used for line markers). The gutter code-action icon is a margin glyph drawn on lines with available actions; clicking it shows a context menu of actions. Define a small provider abstraction (hint -> optional list of code actions) so dialect-specific analyzers (LambdaMoo/ToastStunt/Edgerunner) can contribute. Keep the action execution decoupled from rendering. Reuse the CompletionIconFactory/icon approach for crisp, zoom-aware glyphs (see udd-x6l) if the gutter icon should scale with editor zoom. Likely split into sub-tasks during planning: (a) hint model + provider plumbing on the parse pipeline, (b) hint rendering/markers, (c) gutter action glyph + hit-testing, (d) action menu + first refactorings.
acceptance_criteria: Editor shows non-error hints (info/warning/suggestion) distinct from hard syntax errors, both inline (markers) and discoverable (hover/inline text or the messages page). A gutter/margin icon appears on lines that have available code actions; clicking it opens a menu and selecting an action performs it (at least one working refactoring/quick-fix end to end). Hints and actions are driven by a provider layer so additional analyzers/dialects can contribute without UI changes. Works across all three grammar dialects without regressing existing error reporting.

title: Integrated verb benchmarking tool for fine-tuning
description:
Add an integrated benchmarking tool to the editor so users can profile Moo verb performance directly from the IDE during a fine-tuning workflow.

Goal: let a developer iterate on a verb — make changes, run a benchmark, tweak, re-benchmark — without leaving Moo Udditor or dropping to raw telnet. This tightens the optimization loop for performance-sensitive verbs.

Core capabilities to scope:
- Trigger a benchmark run against a verb on the connected server (e.g. invoke the verb N times / measure ticks/seconds consumed).
- Capture and display timing/tick results in the editor (likely a new dockable page or a panel on the code editor page).
- Allow re-running benchmarks after edits + upload, so before/after results can be compared side by side.
- Optionally persist/track historical results per verb to visualize improvement across iterations.

Open questions to resolve during brainstorming/design:
- How is the verb invoked for benchmarking (server-side eval harness vs. direct call), and how are tick/second costs measured given MOO's resource model?
- Does this need server cooperation (a helper verb/package) or can it be driven purely client-side over the existing connection?
- Where does the UI live (new ManagedPage vs. integrated into MooCodeEditorPage)?
- What metrics matter (wall time, ticks, seconds, memory) and how to present comparisons.
notes: Requested by user 2026-06-08. Workflow envisioned: change verb -> get benchmark -> change -> get benchmark -> repeat for fine tuning. Needs design/brainstorming pass before implementation.

title: Zoom-aware autocomplete popup (scale with Ctrl+wheel editor zoom)
description:
When the Moo Code Editor is zoomed via Ctrl+mouse-wheel (and other zoom paths), the autocomplete popup should scale to match: font, item height, window size, and the category icons + gutter. Icons stay sharp by rendering the CompletionIconFactory ImageList at a 64px base and letting the popup downscale (HighQualityBicubic). FCTB's AutocompleteListView scales font/itemheight/window/gutter/maxheight by tb.Zoom and tracks ZoomChanged; it never generates icons. Full design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-08-zoom-aware-autocomplete-popup-design.md.

Acceptance: zooming the editor in/out scales the autocomplete popup proportionally (text, rows, window, icons, gutter); icons remain crisp through normal zoom range (up to ~400% via 64px downscale); popup is correctly sized whether zoom changed while it was open or closed.
close_reason: Implemented: zoom-aware autocomplete popup scaling across CompletionIconFactory (64px base) and FCTB AutocompleteListView (scaled font/icon/gutter/maxheight + ZoomChanged tracking); new AutocompletePopupMetrics helper with 5 unit tests. Merged to master.

title: Autocomplete popup category icons for the Moo Code Editor
description:
Add small per-entry icons to the Moo Code Editor's autocomplete popup so each completion item shows a category glyph to the left of its text.

In the list view OnPaint (AutocompleteMenu.cs ~482-507) each row reserves an 18px left gutter and draws ImageList.Images[ImageIndex] at (1,y) when ImageList != null && ImageIndex >= 0; text is drawn at x=18.
- It is wired but currently disabled: in MooCodeEditorPage.BuildAutocompleteMenu the items are created with an ImageIndex but the line assigning the ImageList is commented out (//editor.AutocompleteMenu.Items.ImageList = imageList1;). With no ImageList assigned, no icons paint.

Use the existing item types (AutoIndentingSnippet, SnippetAutocompleteItem, etc.) and the category knowledge in MooSyntaxHighlightingGuide / Moo.cs to assign ImageIndex.

title: MCP dev-info query package (IMooWorldQueryProvider impl)
description:
Design and implement a MUD Client Protocol (MCP 2.1) package that provides developer/introspection queries for a connected MOO world, implemented as a concrete IMooWorldQueryProvider (udd-5oh). This is the second provider implementation alongside SDWC (udd-am1).

Note: MCP here = MUD Client Protocol (this codebase's MCP), NOT the LLM Model Context Protocol.

Scope:
- Design the package message set (package name/version, request and response messages) covering the IMooWorldQueryProvider operations: list verbs, list properties, list known objects, list children of an object, get parent, get verb info, get property info.
- Implement the package as an IMcpPackage so it participates in MCP package negotiation (mcp-negotiate).
- Implement IMooWorldQueryProvider on top of the package; register it with the provider-discovery/wiring so it can be bound to an MCP-capable world session.
- Async, with typed result models matching the interface contract.

Dependencies:
- Requires the abstract interface udd-5oh (IMooWorldQueryProvider).
- Requires MCP package negotiation (udd-q2l / feature 4: mcp-negotiate, mcp-cord) so packages can be negotiated and used.

Acceptance:
- A negotiated MCP package exposes verb/property/object/hierarchy queries.
- The package is surfaced as an IMooWorldQueryProvider and can be bound to a session via provider discovery.
- Editor completion/tooltips can consume it identically to the SDWC provider.

Source: user request (design an upcoming MCP package as a second IMooWorldQueryProvider implementation).
close_reason: edgerunner-org-moo-query MCP package implemented: protocol doc, negotiation listener hook, correlator, mapping, provider (13 ops), package class, WindowManager wiring, server dump + INSTALL doc. All reviews passed; merged to master.

title: Abstract dev-info query provider (IMooWorldQueryProvider)
description:
Define an abstracted interface, IMooWorldQueryProvider, that provides a uniform mechanism for querying a connected MOO world for developer/introspection information, independent of the underlying wire protocol. Concrete providers (SDWC, and an upcoming MCP package) implement this interface; the client discovers which providers a given world supports and wires the appropriate one to that MUD world session. Editor windows consume the active provider to power code-completion popups and tooltips.

Interface: IMooWorldQueryProvider
Operations (async-first — most are network round-trips, so return Task/Task<T> with CancellationToken support):
- Query the list of verbs on an object.
- Query the list of properties on an object.
- Query the list of known objects.
- Query the list of all child objects of a given object.
- Query the parent of a given object.
- Query detailed information for a specific verb.
- Query detailed information for a specific property.

Provider model / wiring:
- On connect, attempt to determine which query providers the world supports (capability probe / negotiation).
- Select and bind a provider implementation to the MudWorldSession for that connection.
- Expose the bound provider to editor consumers (completion + tooltips). Gracefully degrade when no provider is available.

Implementations (separate beads):
- SDWC OOB protocol implementation — udd-am1 (becomes an implementation of this interface).
- Upcoming MCP package (to be designed) — a second implementation.

Design notes:
- Keep the interface protocol-agnostic; return typed models (verb info, property info, object id) rather than raw protocol payloads.
- Likely lives in the communication/editor-shared layer so both comms implementations and the editor can reference it.

Acceptance:
- IMooWorldQueryProvider exists with async methods for the seven query operations above.
- At least one concrete implementation can be bound to a session (SDWC, udd-am1).
- Provider discovery selects/binds a supported provider per world session.
- Editor can obtain the active provider and query it for completion/tooltip data.

Source: user request. Related implementations: udd-am1 (SDWC) and a future MCP package bead.
close_reason: Implemented: IMooWorldQueryProvider + models, priority/NotImplementedException-fallthrough registry, per-connection TTL cache, MooWorldQueryService anchored on IMudClientSession, minimal editor accessor hook, and Mud.Common.Tests (27 tests). Independently reviewed; cache sweep timer hardened. Builds clean, all tests pass.

title: Support SDWC protocol for verb/property introspection
description:
Implement client support for the SDWC out-of-band protocol so Udditor can query a connected MOO for an object's verbs and properties and consume the JSON metadata it returns. This provides the live introspection backbone for the object/verb browser and world-aware autocomplete features.

Protocol summary (from docs):
- SDWC is an out-of-band protocol carried over standard MOO output using the #$# OOB prefix (same channel Udditor already handles via OutOfBandMessageProcessor).
- Client -> server requests:
  - #$# SDWC%%VERBS%%<objectId>   (request verbs for an object)
  - #$# SDWC%%PROPS%%<objectId>   (request properties for an object)
- Server -> client responses carry JSON payloads:
  - #$# SDWC%%VERBS%%<json>
  - #$# SDWC%%PROPS%%<json>
- Marker families: control lines, payload responses, and metadata/handshake lines. Payloads are valid JSON.
- Capability toggles (server side, via environment) can disable Object Browser / Property Browser / hover overlays. No formal capability negotiation.

Scope:
- Add an SDWC OOB message handler in the communication layer (register with the OOB pipeline, key off the SDWC%% markers).
- Request API to ask for verbs/props of a given object id; parse and surface the JSON responses as typed models.
- Respect server capability toggles where exposed.
- Expose results to consumers (object/verb browser udd-9ge, world-aware autocomplete udd-of6).

Reference docs:
- https://github.com/SindomeCorp/dome-client/blob/main/docs/SDWC-OOB.md
- Repo docs index: https://github.com/SindomeCorp/dome-client/tree/main/docs

Note: enabler/dependency for udd-9ge (Object / verb browser) and udd-of6 (World-aware autocomplete). Source: user request.
close_reason: SDWC OOB handler, query provider (VERBS/PROPS/overlays), capability detection implemented in fc7dc76; consumed by contextual autocomplete (udd-7g2)

title: Theme editor dialog (View > Theme) with live preview
description:
Add a "Theme" item to the View menu that opens a theme editor dialog exposing the theme/color-related settings in Moo.Editor.config through a GUI, with a live preview, so users can design a color theme without hand-editing the config file.

UI / Design:
- New "Theme" menu entry under the View menu in the main Editor form.
- The dialog uses a horizontal SplitContainer:
  - Left pane: theme settings organized into grouped blocks (by syntax category). Each color setting is editable via the standard Windows color picker (ColorDialog).
  - Right pane: an embedded MooCodeEditor control in read-only mode used purely as a preview.
- The preview editor loads a predefined Moo code sample. The sample is stored in the solution as an embedded text resource (EmbeddedResource) and read at runtime, not loaded from disk.
- Live preview: as the user changes any theme color, the read-only preview editor re-applies syntax highlighting immediately so the user sees the result before applying.
- OK/Apply persists the theme settings back to the active Moo.Editor.config (now in %APPDATA%\Moo Udditor); Cancel discards.

Scope notes:
- Reuse the existing syntax highlighting/colorization pipeline (MooSyntaxHighlightingGuide / Settings) so the preview matches real editor rendering.
- The theme settings here are the color/highlighting subset of config; general editor behavior settings belong to the separate Editor Options dialog (udd-1p9.1).

Acceptance:
- View > Theme opens the dialog with current theme colors populated in grouped blocks.
- Clicking a color opens the standard color selector and updates the value.
- The right-hand read-only preview shows the embedded Moo sample and updates immediately when a color changes.
- Apply writes changes to Moo.Editor.config and they take effect in open editors; Cancel discards.

Source: user request. Sibling of udd-1p9.1 (Editor Options dialog); both expose Moo.Editor.config via UI.
close_reason: Added dark/light mode dropdown, .mood JSON theme import/export (atomic, only-present-keys, monospace font fallback), and converted the dialog to Krypton controls with dialog-local dark/light live preview. Build clean, 29/29 tests pass.

title: Code Editor Enhancements
description: Umbrella epic for features and tasks that improve the Moo code editor tooling — syntax intelligence, verb edit/upload workflow, in-editor diagnostics, navigation/browsing, and autocomplete. Individual editor-related features and tasks should be linked under this epic as children.

title: Feature 11: Per-world color scheme
description:
Each world connection gets its own ANSI color palette and editor theme. When connected to multiple servers simultaneously, the visual distinction makes it immediately obvious which terminal belongs to which server.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#11, Quality of Life)

title: Feature 10: Connection health indicator
description:
A status bar chip showing round-trip latency and bytes in/out per second. Lets the programmer immediately distinguish a slow server from a stuck client.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#10, Quality of Life)

title: Feature 9: World-aware autocomplete
description:
Seed the code editor's autocomplete with verb names, object names, and property names fetched live from the connected server via introspection commands, updated on reconnect.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#9, Quality of Life)

title: Feature 8: Command history persistence
description:
The 15-item command buffer is lost on close. Persist command history per-world to disk across sessions with a configurable depth.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#8, Quality of Life)

title: Feature 7: Inline server error annotation
description:
When the server returns a compile error on verb upload, parse the line number and annotate it directly in the editor gutter with a squiggle and tooltip — same experience as a local compiler.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#7, Editor / Code Intelligence)

title: Feature 6: Object / verb browser
description:
A dockable side panel that issues MOO introspection commands (@show, @list, @props) and populates a tree of objects -> verbs -> properties. Double-click a verb to open it in the code editor.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#6, Editor / Code Intelligence)

title: Feature 5: Verb diff view
description:
When uploading an edited verb, show a diff of the local version vs. the server's current version before sending. Prevents accidental overwrites.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#5, Editor / Code Intelligence)

title: Feature 4: Complete MCP package negotiation
description:
mcp-negotiate and mcp-cord phases of MUD Client Protocol 2.1 are currently unimplemented. Finishing these enables the full round-trip local-edit workflow via MCP rather than the current OOB fallback — a significant improvement for servers that support it.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#4, Editor / Code Intelligence)
close_reason: mcp-negotiate + mcp-cord (the named scope) implemented, wired into WindowManager, and tested (47 passing). Fixed a real FormatMessage quoting bug (now quotes values containing :/*/") and refreshed the stale docs/mcp2-protocol.md status table. The round-trip local-edit workflow that motivated this bead is its own concrete edit package — filed as udd-wm8.

title: Feature 3: Macro / alias system
description:
Define short aliases that expand to full MOO commands, stored per-world in the address book. Support basic variable substitution (%1, %2) and multi-line macros for sequences of commands.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#3, Connectivity & Workflow)

title: Feature 2: Session transcript logging
description:
Opt-in per-world logging of all terminal I/O to a timestamped file. Invaluable for debugging async verb interactions and reproducing intermittent bugs. Configurable via world settings with log rotation by size or date.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#2, Connectivity & Workflow)

title: Feature 1: Linked split connections
description:
Link two terminal connections so they share a single command input. Both connections tile side by side automatically when linked, and any command typed in the shared input bar is transmitted to both servers simultaneously. Output from each server remains independent and visible in its own pane. Useful for testing a verb change across a production and development server at the same time, verifying identical behaviour on two different MOO codebases, or running parallel sessions where commands need to be issued to both worlds in lockstep. Linking and unlinking would be a per-session toggle, with each terminal reverting to its own independent input when unlinked.

Source: docs/feature-suggestions.md (#1, Connectivity & Workflow)

title: Autocomplete: flow-aware lazy reassignment tracking for this/player/caller + locals
description: Follow-up to udd-efk (chained-eval). Resolve the value of a variable used DIRECTLY under the caret (not just as a chain base) when it has been reassigned earlier in the verb, e.g. 'player = #23; ... player:' should complete on #23. Requires a fuller statement-level interpretation of the verb's parse tree along the path from verb start to caret, tracking current values of this/player/caller and arbitrary locals, including branch-reachability awareness (which assignment actually executes). Builds on udd-efk's ChainExpressionEvaluator/LocalVariableResolver/ChainExtractor and reuses the same per-step provider resolution and no-source fallback. Ambiguous/unknown -> no source.

title: Autocomplete: chained member-access expression evaluation (+ minimal var-base tree walk)
description: Resolve chained member-access expressions at the caret so verb/property autocomplete AND hover offer the right object's members. Typing $Mcp.package: evaluates the chain $Mcp -> .package to a concrete object number, then completes members on it. Chain base may be #N, $name, this, player, caller, or a LOCAL VARIABLE. A local-variable base is resolved by a grammar-aware TREE WALK over the verb's ANTLR parse tree to its nearest preceding assignment (any block depth), whose RHS is itself evaluated as a full resolvable chain (recursive, with cycle + depth-8 guards). Three new Editor-library units: ChainExtractor (parse-tree-primary, token fallback), ChainExpressionEvaluator (async recursive), LocalVariableResolver (pure tree walk). Two-layer caching: world-state (objectId,propName) TTL-cached per page; local-variable values NEVER cached (re-derived from live parse tree each request). Swallowed exceptions logged via the existing diagnostic delegate -> Logger.Warn; expected non-resolution stays silent. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-23-chained-expression-evaluation-design.md
notes: Enhancement: the interpreter should also evaluate CHAINED member-access expressions to an object as the completion source. E.g. typing '$Mcp.package:' should evaluate '$Mcp.package' over the current connection (resolve $Mcp -> #0.Mcp's object value, then read property '.package' on that object); if the result is an object number, use that # as the source to fetch available verbs/properties for. So the walker resolves operand chains of the form <base>.prop[.prop...] where <base> may be $name / #N / this / player / caller / a local variable, evaluating each step via the provider's property-value query, then completes members on the final resolved object. Non-object / unresolved steps fall back to no-source.

title: IMcpPackage interface polish: read-only Name/version properties, Reset() contract
description: Inherited 2022-era design flaws noted in udd-btl Task 6 review: (1) IMcpPackage.Name/MinimumVersion/MaximumVersion are get;set; — mutating Name would desynchronize the dispatcher registration key from the const PackageName each package matches on in CanHandleMessage; should be get-only. (2) Reset() exists on packages with <inheritdoc/> but is not declared on IMcpPackage or IMcpProtocolHandler and is never called — either add it to the interface (and call on disconnect, see related teardown bug) or delete it everywhere.

value: Color-picker gotcha (magenta): magenta (FF00FF) is commonly used as a transparency MASK key in WinForms/GDI. On a prior project, a color swatch BUTTON whose BackColor was set to magenta rendered transparent, and the ColorDialog broke when seeded from it. Mitigation pattern used in ThemeEditorDialog: the swatch is an owner-drawn ColorSwatch control that paints the color via SolidBrush in OnPaint (never via control BackColor), and the ColorDialog is seeded from the stored setting value (get()), not from the swatch control. For any NEW color-picker UI, do NOT drive a swatch fill through a control's BackColor and do NOT seed the ColorDialog from the control -- otherwise magenta will render/behave as transparent.

Design rule (Thad, emphatic): verb/property SUMMARY listings (GetVerbsAsync/GetPropertiesAsync and any wire payloads behind them) care about the QUERIED object only — do NOT carry or design in per-row defining-object data. Client-side summary records fill DefiningObject with the queried object id. Resolved/defining-object semantics are legitimate ONLY where the IMooWorldQueryProvider contract explicitly models them: GetVerbInfoAsync, GetVerbDocumentationAsync, GetVerbCodeAsync (QueriedObjectId/ResolvedObjectId pairs).

Workflow: close the relevant bead BEFORE committing, so the bead-state change (.beads/issues.jsonl) lands in the SAME commit as the code/work it relates to. Do not commit the code first and close the bead afterward — that strands the bead closure (and any follow-on label/archive changes) in separate trailing commits.
